review_evidence: All 1710 listed paths resolve in reservoir-sources/Vilin97__lean-pool and every on-disk byte size equals the size in the brief.

A case-insensitive grep for theorem|lemma|def |structure|class|instance|inductive|abbrev|example|axiom|elab|noncomputable|macro|syntax finds no match in exactly 3 files: FormalizationOfBoundedArithmetic/SimpRules.lean, FormalizationOfBoundedArithmetic/Register.lean, and CircuitComplexity/AON.lean. All three were read in full.

LeanPool/FormalizationOfBoundedArithmetic/Register.lean (703 bytes) holds `register_simp_attr delta0_simps`, which declares the simp set used throughout the bounded-arithmetic development. This is an executable command, so the file is outside FILTER-007 and is retained.

LeanPool/FormalizationOfBoundedArithmetic/SimpRules.lean (566 bytes, the smallest file) holds `attribute [delta0_simps]` for Sum.elim_inl, Sum.swap_inl, Function.comp_apply, and other lemmas. Attribute commands take it outside FILTER-007, so it is retained.

LeanPool/FormalizationOfBoundedArithmetic/MathlibSimps.lean has no top-level theorem or def but holds an `elab "mkDelta0FromModelTheory" : command` metaprogram and its invocation, which adds Mathlib model-theory simp lemmas to delta0_simps. It is retained.

A comment-stripped scan that accepts only module, import, public/meta import, and prelude lines matches no file in the unit. When `@[expose] public section`, namespace, and end lines are also allowed, it matches only LeanPool/CircuitComplexity/AON.lean and LeanPool/CircuitComplexity/LowerBound.lean.

LeanPool/CircuitComplexity/AON.lean and LeanPool/CircuitComplexity/LowerBound.lean were read in full. Both are re-export modules with long module docstrings that name the main results (CompleteBasis Basis.unboundedAON; Circuit.gate_elimination_lower_bound, whose full statement is in the docstring). Both also contain `@[expose] public section` and `namespace CircuitComplexity` / `end CircuitComplexity`. FILTER-007 puts namespace and section commands outside its unilateral class, and the docstrings are the search phrases a user knows, so both are retained.

The largest files are genuine proof content: NavierStokesAndEuler/NavierStokes/CorrectionStep.lean (595,864 bytes, 420 top-level theorem/lemma/def lines), CorrectionInitialization.lean (324,372 bytes, 254), and ActualCandidateAssembly.lean (192,324 bytes, 242).
The small NavierStokesAndEuler/ForMathlib/SmoothnessOrder.lean (692 bytes) was read in full. It proves `le_infinity_iff_ne_top` on WithTop ℕ∞ and is retained.

A junk-signal grep (lorem|ipsum|placeholder|dummy|foobar) hits 6 files. Each hit is mathematical prose on real declarations: Euler/Solution.lean and SolutionDefinitions.lean say they avoid the reference placeholder theorem; ActualSignedPhysicalBinding.lean describes a 'dummy band index'; SlowBorelBase.lean describes a zero placeholder at index zero.

The TODO/FIXME/XXX grep hits 7 files, all in FormalizationOfBoundedArithmetic (Complexity, IDelta0, IOPEN, LanguageZambella, Order, Semantics, Syntax). Each hit is a developer note on a real proof or definition. `grep -w sorry` matches no file in the unit.

Per-subdirectory samples show real mathematics: MarshallHall/MarshallHall.lean (rank_freeProduct_eq_add), Rado/Complex/PlanarConnected.lean (isPathConnected_ball_diff_two_disks), Erdos1196/FirstEntryRowTerm.lean (entryThreshold, firstEntryTail), FourAP/Binary.lean, Sabidussi/CyclicWord.lean (structure Word), FactorizationSystems/Characterization.lean (isReplete), RootSystem/BCn.lean (dotProduct), Erdos81PaperIContrib/FgConeClosed.lean (conic_caratheodory), Euler/AllOrderCorrectionCoherence.lean (correction_limit_equation), ForMathlib/FiniteSum.lean (sum_le_sum_of_injOn).
summary: Reviewed all 1710 listed Lean files under LeanPool (NavierStokesAndEuler 1584, CircuitComplexity 26, MarshallHall 25, FormalizationOfBoundedArithmetic 20, Rado 14, Erdos1196 13, FourAP 10, Sabidussi 9, FactorizationSystems 5, RootSystem 2, Erdos81PaperIContrib 2) by byte-size verification, declaration-keyword grep, a comment-stripped import-only scan, junk and TODO greps, and per-subdirectory sampling. About 49,700 top-level declarations were counted, no file uses sorry, and no file is a pure import-only module: the two closest candidates carry `@[expose] public section` plus namespace commands, and the other declaration-free files register or populate simp attributes. Every file stays searchable; rules is empty.

summary: Inspected all 5 changed/added Lean files. Each contains substantial formal mathematical content: definitions, theorems, proofs, and inductive types. None are pure import aggregators, junk, or documentation-only. NF.lean has circuit embeddings and lower bound theorems; Complexity.lean defines complexity classes (IsDelta0, IsSigma0B) with relabeling theorems; IDelta0.lean formalizes IΔ₀ arithmetic models with induction theorems; Hall.lean proves the Marshall Hall finite-core completion; Separation.lean constructs finite permutation separators for free group subgroup separability.
